newsitem.title: USA: AHP says Q4 pharm sales up, health care off.
newsitem.headline: AHP says Q4 pharm sales up, health care off.

text.p: American Health Products Corp Tuesday said U.S. pharmaceutical sales increased 15 percent in the fourth quarter on 1996, and 11 percent for the full year.
But U.S. consumer health care sales fell 6 percent for the 1996 fourth quarter and increased 2 percent for the full year.

The pharmaceutical sales gains were due primarily to higher sales of anti-obesity products Redux and Pondimin, Premarin products, recombinant Factor VIII and Naprelan. Higher sales of Lodine also contributed to the increase, the company said.
But the gains were offset, in part, by lower sales of certain cardiovascular products.

The decrease in consumer health care sales was due primarily to lower sales of Orudis KT related to its 1995 fourth quarter launch, Advil and cough and cold products. The slump was offset, in part, by introductory sales of Axid AR and higher sales of Centrum, the company said.
